comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Loan Portfolio Composition and Credit Quality Statistics
comparisons.peer_summary: The company presents outstanding consumer loans, nonperforming loans, and past-due accruals in Table 19, with outstandings primarily consisting of auto and specialty lending ($54.9 billion), U.S. securities-based lending ($48.7 billion), and non-U.S. consumer loans ($2.8 billion) at December 31, 2024. Residential mortgage loans include fully-insured loans with curtailed interest, and the company excludes fully-insured and fair-value-option loans from certain credit quality statistics to better represent ongoing operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose the geographic and product scope of their consumer loan delinquency metrics. Citi explicitly defines its 'Asia Consumer' segment to include loans from Poland and Russia for all periods presented, while noting the exclusion of certain sold businesses like Taiwan and Indonesia. Similarly, Bank of America presents its consumer loan outstandings and delinquency statistics, specifying that non-U.S. consumer loans constitute a distinct component ($2.8 billion) of its total portfolio alongside U.S.-based auto, specialty, and securities-based lending. Both disclosures clarify which geographic or product segments are included or excluded from their respective credit quality tables to ensure accurate representation of ongoing operations.
